readings.title_ar: How extreme weather events are changing our world

paragraphs: Every year, millions of people around the world experience the incredible power of extreme weather. From massive sandstorms that *sweep across* desert regions to powerful hurricanes that *devastate* coastal cities, these natural events remind us how small we are compared to nature's force.

Climate scientists have been studying these phenomena for decades, and they are discovering some *alarming* patterns. Dr. Sarah Ahmed, a meteorologist at King Abdullah University, explains that extreme weather events are becoming more *frequent* and more intense. "We're seeing temperatures that *break records* almost every summer," she says. "Last year, parts of the Arabian Peninsula experienced temperatures above 50°C for fifteen consecutive days." These *scorching* heat waves were affecting daily life across the region, while people were trying to stay cool indoors during the hottest parts of the day.

However, extreme weather isn't just about heat. In 2022, unusual flooding *struck* several areas in Saudi Arabia, causing significant damage to infrastructure. The rain was *pouring down* so heavily that streets became rivers within hours. Emergency teams were working around the clock to help families who had been *trapped* in their homes. These events show us that even desert regions can experience unexpected water-related disasters.

Looking toward the future, scientists are developing better *prediction* systems to help communities prepare for extreme weather. New technology is being installed across the Kingdom to monitor weather patterns more accurately. "We want to give people enough warning time so they can take *shelter* and protect their families," explains Dr. Ahmed. The government is also planning to build more weather-resistant buildings and improve emergency response systems.

The message is clear: extreme weather events are becoming part of our reality. While we cannot control nature's power, we can prepare for it. By understanding these patterns and investing in better infrastructure, communities can become more resilient when the next storm, heat wave, or unexpected weather event arrives.

readings.critical_thinking_prompt_en: How might the increasing frequency of extreme weather events change the way people plan their daily lives and design their cities in the future?

readings.title_ar: The science behind the Middle East's most powerful sandstorms

paragraphs: The sky was *turning* dark orange as Ahmed pulled over his car on the highway outside Riyadh. Within minutes, a massive wall of sand was *approaching* the city at 60 kilometers per hour. This wasn't just any ordinary dust—it was a haboob, one of nature's most spectacular and dangerous weather phenomena that regularly *affects* the Arabian Peninsula.

Haboobs are giant sandstorms that *occur* when strong winds from thunderstorms pick up loose sand and dust from desert surfaces. These towering walls of sand can reach heights of 1,500 meters and stretch across hundreds of kilometers. While Ahmed was experiencing this storm, meteorologists at the King Abdulaziz City for Science and Technology were *monitoring* its movement using advanced satellite technology. The storm had *originated* in the Empty Quarter and was moving northeast toward populated areas.

The frequency of these extreme weather events has been *increasing* in recent years. Climate scientists have recorded that the Arabian Peninsula now experiences 30% more sandstorms compared to two decades ago. Dr. Fatima Al-Rashid, a meteorologist at King Saud University, explains that rising temperatures are *causing* stronger wind patterns. "When the ground becomes extremely hot, it creates more *turbulence* in the atmosphere," she notes. "This turbulence helps *generate* the powerful winds that lift sand particles high into the air."

These storms *pose* serious challenges for modern life in Saudi Arabia. Airports frequently cancel flights, and hospitals report increased cases of respiratory problems during sandstorm seasons. The government has been *implementing* new warning systems to help citizens prepare for approaching storms. Weather stations now send text messages to mobile phones when dangerous conditions are developing.

Looking toward the future, scientists are developing better *forecasting* methods to predict when and where these storms will strike. New research suggests that by understanding wind patterns over the Arabian Desert, meteorologists can provide warnings up to 48 hours in advance. This early warning system will help protect both residents and the millions of pilgrims who visit Saudi Arabia each year, ensuring their safety during these dramatic displays of nature's power.

listening.title_en: Talking About an Incoming Sandstorm and Changed Plans
listening.title_ar: محادثة عن عاصفة رملية قادمة وتغيير الخطط
listening.transcript:
Layla: Hi Noor! You look worried. What's wrong?

Noor: Oh, Layla! I was watching the weather news, and they're predicting a huge sandstorm for this weekend. It's going to be much worse than the one we had last month.

Layla: Really? That's concerning. What were you planning to do this weekend?

Noor: Well, I was going to visit my sister in Dammam, but now I think I'll have to cancel. The roads will be too dangerous. What about you? Were you planning anything special?

Layla: Yes, actually. My family and I were going to have a picnic in the park, but we'll definitely stay home now. Last time during the sandstorm, we were sitting inside all day while the wind was howling outside. It was quite scary.

Noor: I remember that day! The visibility was terrible, and everyone was driving so slowly. My brother was coming home from work, and it took him three hours instead of one.

Layla: That sounds awful. You know, I think sandstorms are becoming more frequent than before. My grandmother says they didn't have such strong ones when she was young.

Noor: That's true. Climate change is making extreme weather more common everywhere. Speaking of weather, did you hear about the floods in Jeddah last week?

Layla: Yes, it was on the news every day. The rain was much heavier than usual, and many streets were completely flooded. Some people were trapped in their cars while the water was rising around them.

Noor: It's frightening how unpredictable weather is becoming. One day we have flooding, the next day we have sandstorms, and in summer the heat waves are more intense than ever.

Layla: Exactly. I'm going to start checking the weather forecast more carefully. I think we all need to be better prepared for these extreme conditions.

Noor: Good idea. I'm also going to buy some emergency supplies this week - water, flashlights, and non-perishable food. It's better to be safe than sorry.

Layla: That's smart thinking. Maybe we should encourage our friends to prepare too. We can share tips on social media about staying safe during extreme weather.

Noor: Perfect! We'll help everyone stay informed and ready.

She heard there will be a big sandstorm this weekend.
She had a terrible argument with her sister in Dammam and does not know how to fix things.
She missed work.

wrong_notes.0: فيضانات جدة ذُكرت لاحقًا في الحديث كخبر الأسبوع الماضي، وليست سبب قلق نور في البداية.
wrong_notes.2: التسجيل لم يذكر أي خلاف مع الأخت، فزيارة الدمام أُلغيت بسبب خطورة الطرق لا بسبب شجار.
wrong_notes.3: لم يرد في الحوار أي شيء عن العمل، فقلق نور جاء من توقعات عاصفة رملية قوية.

exercises.explanation_ar: أخبرت نور لَيلى أنها كانت تشاهد نشرة الطقس وأنهم يتوقعون عاصفة رملية ضخمة هذا الأسبوع، لذلك كانت قلقة.

hint.quote: My family and I were going to have a picnic in the park, but we'll definitely stay home now.
hint.answer_phrase: have a picnic in the park

options: Have a picnic in the park.
Visit Noor.
Go shopping.
Stay home.
exercises.question_en: What was Layla's family planning to do this weekend before they heard about the sandstorm?

wrong_notes.1: زيارة نور لم تُذكر في خطط ليلى، فالتسجيل قال إن عائلتها خططت لنزهة في الحديقة.
wrong_notes.2: التسوق لم يرد في الحوار إطلاقًا، فالخطة الأصلية كانت نزهة عائلية في الحديقة.
wrong_notes.3: البقاء في المنزل هو القرار الجديد بعد سماع خبر العاصفة، وليس الخطة الأصلية للعائلة.

exercises.explanation_ar: قالت لَيلى إن عائلتها كانت تخطط للذهاب في نزهة في الحديقة، لكنهم قرروا البقاء في المنزل بسبب العاصفة.

hint.quote: I was watching the weather news, and they're predicting a huge sandstorm for this weekend. It's going to be much worse than the one we had last month.
hint.answer_phrase: much worse than the one we had last month

options: Floods in Jeddah last month → sandstorm last week → heat wave this weekend → heavy rain yesterday
Heat wave last summer → sandstorm last month → floods in Jeddah this weekend → blizzard next week
Sandstorm last month → floods in Jeddah last week → sandstorm this weekend
Sandstorm last week → floods in Jeddah last month → another sandstorm earlier this year → heat wave
exercises.question_en: What is the correct order of weather events mentioned in the conversation?

wrong_notes.0: هذا الترتيب يضع الفيضانات الشهر الماضي ويضيف موجة حر ومطرًا لم يذكرهما الحوار بهذا التوقيت.
wrong_notes.1: التسجيل لم يذكر موجة حر الصيف الماضي ولا عاصفة ثلجية، والفيضانات كانت الأسبوع الماضي لا نهاية الأسبوع.
wrong_notes.3: هذا يعكس التوقيتات، فالعاصفة السابقة كانت الشهر الماضي والفيضانات الأسبوع الماضي وليس العكس.

exercises.explanation_ar: ذكرت نور أولاً العاصفة الرملية الشهر الماضي، ثم تحدثتا عن فيضانات جدة الأسبوع الماضي، والعاصفة القادمة هذا الأسبوع.

hint.quote: The visibility was terrible, and everyone was driving so slowly. My brother was coming home from work, and it took him three hours instead of one.
hint.answer_phrase: visibility was terrible, and everyone was driving so slowly

options: His car broke down on the highway.
He had to stop and wait for several hours at his office because the roads were completely closed by police due to the dangerous weather conditions.
He got lost trying a new route home.
The visibility was very poor and everyone was driving slowly.
exercises.question_en: Why did it take Noor's brother three hours to get home from work during the last sandstorm?

wrong_notes.0: التسجيل لم يذكر تعطل السيارة، بل قالت نور إن الرؤية كانت سيئة والجميع يقود ببطء.
wrong_notes.1: لم يرد في الحوار أي إغلاق للطرق من الشرطة أو انتظار في المكتب، فالسبب كان بطء القيادة وسوء الرؤية.
wrong_notes.2: الضياع في طريق جديد لم يُذكر إطلاقًا، فالتأخير سببه الرؤية السيئة والقيادة البطيئة.

exercises.explanation_ar: أوضحت نور أن الرؤية كانت سيئة جداً وأن الجميع كان يقود ببطء شديد، مما جعل رحلة أخيها تستغرق ثلاث ساعات بدلاً من ساعة واحدة.

hint.quote: I'm also going to buy some emergency supplies this week - water, flashlights, and non-perishable food. It's better to be safe than sorry.
hint.answer_phrase: buy some emergency supplies this week

options: It is better to prepare ahead of time to avoid problems later.
You should always feel sorry for people who did not prepare for bad weather events.
Staying safe costs money.
It is wiser to stay home and avoid all risks rather than going out and regretting your decision when something unexpected and dangerous happens.
exercises.question_en: What does Noor mean when she says 'It's better to be safe than sorry'?

wrong_notes.1: العبارة لا تعني الشفقة على غير المستعدين، بل تعني الاستعداد المسبق لتجنب المشكلات لاحقًا.
wrong_notes.2: الحديث عن التكلفة المادية لم يرد في السياق، فنور تقصد أن الاحتياط المبكر خير من الندم.
wrong_notes.3: حصر المعنى في البقاء بالمنزل وتجنب كل المخاطر أضيق من المقصود، فالسياق عن شراء مستلزمات الطوارئ استعدادًا.

exercises.explanation_ar: تعني هذه العبارة أنه من الأفضل الاستعداد مسبقاً لتجنب المشاكل، وهو ما قصدته نور عند حديثها عن شراء مستلزمات الطوارئ.

hint.quote: You know, I think sandstorms are becoming more frequent than before. My grandmother says they didn't have such strong ones when she was young.
hint.answer_phrase: they didn't have such strong ones when she was young

options: They are rare.
They are harmless.
Sandstorms have become stronger or more common over time.
They are seasonal.
exercises.question_en: What does Layla's grandmother's comment suggest about sandstorms?

wrong_notes.0: الندرة عكس المقصود، فتعليق الجدة استُخدم دليلًا على أن العواصف صارت أقوى مما كانت.
wrong_notes.1: الحوار كله يصور العواصف خطرًا حقيقيًا على الطرق والرؤية، فوصفها بغير المؤذية يناقض التسجيل.
wrong_notes.3: الموسمية لم تُذكر في كلام الجدة، فمغزاه أن العواصف القوية لم تكن موجودة في شبابها.

exercises.explanation_ar: قول جدة لَيلى إنه لم تكن هناك عواصف رملية قوية كهذه في شبابها يُشير إلى أن العواصف أصبحت أشد وأكثر تكراراً مع مرور الوقت.

hint.quote: Perfect! We'll help everyone stay informed and ready.
hint.answer_phrase: help everyone stay informed and ready

options: They want to gain more followers and increase their popularity on social media platforms.
They feel responsible for helping their community stay informed and safe.
They were specifically asked by local authorities and emergency services to spread safety information.
They hope to start a well-known community organization dedicated to extreme weather preparedness and relief.
exercises.question_en: At the end of the conversation, what is the MAIN reason Layla and Noor decide to share tips on social media?

wrong_notes.0: التسجيل لم يذكر متابعين أو شهرة، فالهدف المعلن مساعدة الأصدقاء على البقاء آمنين ومطلعين.
wrong_notes.2: لا وجود في الحوار لأي طلب من جهات رسمية أو دفاع مدني، فالمبادرة جاءت من الصديقتين نفسيهما.
wrong_notes.3: تأسيس منظمة مجتمعية لم يُطرح إطلاقًا، فالفكرة اقتصرت على مشاركة نصائح السلامة عبر مواقع التواصل.

exercises.explanation_ar: يتضح من حديث لَيلى ونور أنهما تشعران بالمسؤولية تجاه مجتمعهما، وترغبان في مساعدة الأصدقاء على الاستعداد للطقس القاسي، وليس لأي هدف شخصي أو توجيه رسمي.
